transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because since I moved into this busted-up room, I’ve been on edge. I’m up late dealing with leaks and the heat, then I’m dragging myself to work late and messing up things I normally handle. I’ve been snapping at people too.
Are you having trouble falling asleep?
Yeah. I’m up late a lot dealing with the leaks or the heat in that room, and then I can’t get settled down.
Do you feel on edge mainly because of the problems with that room?

Yeah, mostly. Ever since I moved into that room, it’s been one thing after another—leaks, heat, staying up trying to deal with it. Then I’m tired at work, late, messing up stuff I usually don’t, and I’ve been snapping at people.
If the leaks and heat in the room were fixed, do you think you would still have trouble sleeping?
I don’t think so, not like this. If I wasn’t up dealing with the leaks and that heat, I’d probably be able to settle down and sleep.
Did these problems start after you moved into that room?
Yeah. I was doing pretty normal before I moved in there. Within the first couple weeks, once I found the water damage and the heat problems, that’s when all this started.
Has this situation been causing problems for you at work?
Yeah. I’ve had paperwork and scheduling problems already, and my foreman told me I could lose my chance at moving toward crew lead if I keep slipping like this.
Has this situation been causing you a lot of emotional distress?
Yeah, a lot. I’m stressed out all the time about that room, and I’ve been snapping at people more than I normally would. It’s messing with everything.
Do you feel isolated or like you don't have people you can rely on right now?
I’m not really sure what you mean. I mean, I’ve got people around, but I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about relying on anybody right now.
Aside from the problems with that room, have you been feeling on edge about other things too?
I’m not sure. Mostly it’s just that situation that’s been getting to me.
Do you feel like the stress from that room is what’s causing these problems?

Yeah. Ever since I moved into that busted-up room, I’ve been snapping at people and staying up trying to deal with leaks or the heat. Then I’m exhausted, late to work, and messing up things I normally handle fine.
When you have a night away from that room, do you still have trouble sleeping?
Yeah, usually I sleep better if I’m not there. It’s the leaks and the heat stuff that keeps me up, trying to deal with it.
When you’re away from that room, do you still feel on edge?
Not really. When I’m away from it, I’m usually okay. It’s being there, dealing with all that stuff, that gets me wound up.
Do you feel your reaction to the problems with that room has been stronger than most people would have in the same situation?
I’m not sure. It feels like a lot to me, but I don’t know how other people would handle it.
Before you moved into that room, were you having trouble sleeping?
No, I was doing pretty normal before I moved in there. The sleep trouble started in the first couple weeks, after I found the water damage and the heat problems.
When you have a chance to sleep in a comfortable place, do you still have trouble sleeping?
No, if I’m somewhere comfortable, I sleep okay. It’s when I’m up dealing with the leaks or the heat in that room that I end up staying awake.
